paragraphs.text: And the synagogues and houses will be holy and well ordered, because the one who made many people like animals has not entered them.
Those who cast these words away from themselves are the people who do not pray that the abyss may not swallow them.
These are the people who have not taken these thoughts to heart so that they might turn to their God.
There is a word or a deed that has caused sorrow, so that they might turn to their God.
There is a word or deed that has caused a child grief through his parents, because he used to quarrel with them.
God will not send him down upon us. Again, [?] will not escape him.

This is why, perhaps, just as Rebekah was eager for Jacob to receive the blessing from his father because he obeyed them, the good child will receive the blessing from God, Jesus, because he submits to him and obeys his mother, the church, and the wicked child will be excluded from it, because he quarrels with her through his evil deeds, like Esau.
There are firstborn children who inherit from their parents because they obey them.
And there are younger children who are excluded from the inheritance because they are disobedient. There are also younger children who inherit because of their good conduct.
And there are older children who are excluded from the inheritance because of their disobedience.
I have said these things in this way.
It is for you yourselves to judge who is the older
and who is the younger—not because it is difficult for me to say whether it is the priest or the layperson,
but rather because a person wants to convince himself through the delusion of his heart, even if he is excluded from the kingdom of heaven rather than truly being welcomed and entering it.
Again, there is a mother whose firstborn children live with her in the house to care for her,
while the children born after them are in the field, working and bringing things home to her, and she has many good things.

Who would not say that, if she becomes angry with those living with her because of the insults they direct at her, she will hide these things from them until the others come home and then give them to those?
And again, if those assigned to do what is needed in the house give them relief, she will give these things to them.
And if the others come home to her, she will hide these things from them because they have angered her by doing things she does not want.
If, then, we have understood that those words refer to the church, the priests as older children, and the laypeople as younger children, we need no explanation.
May we receive a blessing from God, and not receive rebukes and insults.
If nothing is good and nothing is pleasant except for brothers to live together in one place, while they are still on earth,

And other evil thoughts also intrude upon them. yet they do not welcome one another, then how much better and sweeter it is for us, fathers and children together, to be worthy to gather in that one place, which is the kingdom of heaven.
To whom does this great wealth belong?
Does it belong to the priest in his rank, or to the monk, or else to the layperson?

I know nothing except what the Lord said: “It belongs to those for whom it has been prepared by my Father,” through their hardships and their good deeds, and not, instead, through places, a name, or outward appearance.
These things will not benefit a person without deeds.
I said on another occasion that [?] this report: some had fallen onto the altar because of drunkenness and the frenzy caused by wine, and they were lying prostrate in that place.
It is disgraceful to speak of these things and shameful to hear about them.
Others are caught breaking into houses and people’s premises [?], stealing and speaking other idle words and blasphemies.
If the priest will not begin doing deeds that please God—deeds that are excellent, good, perfect, and holy—who will do them?
But there are many who do his will in complete purity and complete truth, to our shame.
The Scriptures themselves command the people to bring us good offerings containing no impurity or defilement.
“For every choice offering of yours,” he said, “all the first produce from all your firstfruits, will belong to the priests.
And you shall give the priests the first portion of what you eat, so that the blessing may come upon your house.”
And there is nothing about which they have not said that the priests are to take from it first.
But we, for our part, neglect to do what is right.
Or will we really escape the threat in these words: “Those who hate justice and pervert everything that is right”?

Who are those about whom this voice says, “God has stood in the assembly of the gods, and in their midst he will judge the gods, saying, ‘How long will you [?] injustice and show favoritism to sinners?’”—if not everyone who holds high office under God, each according to his rank?
People who are called gods, then, ought to do deeds befitting the title of the high offices of the one who said,
“I said, ‘You are gods, and you are all sons of the Most High,’” lest, because of their contempt,
he say, “Look, you will die like human beings,
and you will fall like one of the rulers,” meaning, “You will fall like one of the pagans,” or, “You will die like the pagans and all heretics.”
Or is this not clear in the Scriptures: when many of those holding high office under God turned justice into gall,
and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness, they fell like the rulers of the nations, whom God had all destroyed from the beginning?
What benefit did Saul gain at the time when he rejected the word of God?
He fell from the favor of the one who had honored him by making him king, and he also fell in the battle against the Philistines.

I have not cited this one alone as indisputable testimony that many have fallen since the beginning of time, despite the title “god” and “son of the Most High.” And after they were appointed as judges, like those two elders who died like godless people because Daniel caught them in their evil deeds. And like Nadab and Abihu, who died like people who know neither God nor his judgments and commandments, and like those who serve other gods, which are not gods at all, made of wood and stone.
And I wish that this statement did not apply to many of you—for I will say not “many of you,” but “most.”
For look, you will die like those who do not know Jesus, and you will fall like those who worship Cronus.
This is the great disgrace that we have boldly incurred.
Or should everyone who wants to do good envy us when they see our righteous deeds, or should people speak about our evil deeds?
Or should they reflect on the love we have for one another?
Or should we be known for purity and freedom?
Or should you be known for defilement and acts of robbery, and lies and false oaths?
And this other old hypocrisy and this human praise: not only do we tolerate them, but we even fight on their behalf when they are caught doing demonic deeds.
The faithful and
the holy ones among you have gone about groaning, filled with suffering and torment because of these vile deeds.

Because of you they are ashamed before those rejected by God, namely the pagans, and before all those who do what was said about him: “Record this man as a man who has been rejected, [?] his name and honor extinguished on earth,” as it is written of the children of Cronus and the slaves of Satan. Those who chew on thoughts and demonic ideas like tree roots, because of their great hunger for the word of the Scriptures and the divinity of this Almighty One, because of their great hunger for the bread that came down from heaven, Jesus,
For they will sit speaking against us, laughing, mocking, and adding to what they hear, just as they can devise every kind of evil against us through the malice of their father, the devil.
But the wisdom of these words comes to us from the Lord: “If salt loses its taste, with what will it be salted?”

It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile, even though every kind of bad thing, or things that rot, are thrown onto it. Likewise, it is Hades that will inherit those who die in their sins.
He is of no use to the house of God, nor even to the world.
He is of no use, so that the devil is more righteous than he is.
Nor is he any use in causing a sinner to repent because of him.
He holds back the Christian who resembles him in perversity and [?] weakness.
He is a stumbling block to those who want to know God.
Where do they throw him out?
Or where? He is thrown out of the holy places to return to the place he came from, like Judas, who returned to his own house.
He is thrown out into the darkness of which the Gospel spoke.
Even if we have not now been thrown out of God's places because of the evil things we do,
who, then, will leave us in them when death makes us strangers to them?
Let us be afraid that God may hide his face from us in this place of exile, just as he said to those people at that time: “Because of the sins they committed against me, I hid my face from them.
I handed them over to those who oppressed them.
And they all fell by the sword. According to their impurities and according to the deeds they had done,
I repaid them. I hid my face from them.”

People who are lifted up by the Spirit of the Lord and brought into the courtyard—or the courtyards—and made to stand in them to see the glory of God in his house, and people whom unclean spirits make behave lewdly through the deception of bitter passions in the courtyards of his holy place!
What can we say?
Or what will we say before those people—I mean all the saints?
Or how ashamed will we be on the day of their boldness, which they now have in heaven with the angels, because they also acted boldly while living on earth?

Listen, and let us fear the one who fills heaven and fills the earth, and who fills his house even more. Then we, whose hearts are closed, may understand that those who see these great wonders of God are not careless.
The thought apart from deeds

They are not empty like us. They will not contemplate heavenly things in every matter and also do earthly things like us. They will not be companions of angels, who call them “greatly loved men,” and also be companions of people who sacrifice to demons, as some among us sit laughing with them, making jokes and shouting.
“Now a spirit,” said the [?] prophet Ezekiel, one of those who often saw the mystery of the glory of the one who is exalted and blessed,
“lifted me up and brought me into the inner courtyard.
And look, the glory of the Lord filled the house.
And I heard someone speaking to me from inside the house.
And a man was standing beside me.
He said to me, ‘Son of man, you have seen the place of my throne, where I sit, and the place where I set my feet, the place where I will dwell forever among the children of Israel.

And let [?] and their kings, through their prostitution and through the abominations of their kings in their death, when they set my seat beside my seat, and their dwelling place beside my dwelling place, with the wall standing between me and them.
And they defiled my holy name with the abominations they committed.
And I destroyed them in my anger.
Now, then, let them put their prostitution far away from me, along with the murders committed by their kings, and I will live among them forever.

Or let us feel shame before people, so that the salt does not become tasteless and get thrown out and trampled by people, as he said—that is, so that they do not ridicule us, insult us, and humiliate us,
saying, “Are these the people who are thought to live with the angels?”

Or let us feel shame before the saints, as though they were beside us now, lest we be unable to escape their rebuke for our foolishness on the day when we see them face to face and they say these words to us:
“These are the salt of the earth who came after us!”
And, “These are the light of the world!”
And, “Words, but no freedom!”
Perhaps now you will find someone guarding himself against these evil blows.
If only you would stay with me a few more days! We would benefit you with very, very many other good things.
But we will take our fill of them in the place where we will never be separated from one another, when our Lord Jesus Christ makes us worthy,
to whom belong every good thing and every act of mercy.
and to whom belong compassion and forgiveness,
and whose will is merciful, and who forgets impiety,
And he covers the sins of all who will repent.

And he will throw all our lawless deeds into the depths of the sea, so that they never appear at all, so that they do not appear, and so that they are not brought forward against us, and so that we are not judged because of them, just as his voice, full of love for humanity, said: “I will wipe away your sins; I will not remember them.”

For if what the holy apostle said were not true—“Although I am not beside you in body, I am with you in spirit”— every friend and everyone who loves people would be deeply distressed because they do not see their loved ones until they meet one another in the body.
In this way, brothers never truly part from one another in their hearts.

And just as Jesus is beside everyone who loves God, yet they do not see him until the day when he makes them worthy to see him face to face, so everyone who loves people and everyone who loves their brothers is beside one another in spirit until the time when we meet one another in person.
For there are people who live together in the body but are not beside one another in their hearts, just as evil exists in many places.
What kind of love do these people have?
A discourse following this, which he delivered before these same people again, together with those who had joined them:

There are kinds of people who dig holes in dung heaps and other places, searching in the earth until they find tiny amounts of gold and silver, or copper, or even something worth less than these, down to potsherds, searching until they find their livelihood.
But our life is revealed to us. It is within us; it is close to us; we know it; it is before us. We are taught to become rich in it, and yet most of us are poor.

People like these search. Sometimes they find what they are looking for; sometimes they do not find it. But we will not search; we hesitate. that perhaps we will not find the one we are seeking. Jesus, who is life in its fullness, lives with those who hope in him, without question.
As the holy apostle said, “Do you not recognize that Jesus Christ is in you—unless perhaps you are worthless?”
You see that the whole treasure, which is Christ, is hidden within us. We only need to stir ourselves toward him now; we only need to uncover his face now, especially since he is not far away.
This is what this means: all we need to do is endure a little hardship; all we need to do is awaken him within us; all we need to do is open our heart to him.
There is a kind of device that the people we mentioned throw into the depths. It wraps itself around the gold and silver until those searching in the murky water find it.

You too, O person who is being sought through the Scriptures’ calls to repent, let the word of God wrap itself around you and take hold of you, until those searching for you draw you up out of the mire of sin. Then there will be joy for the one speaking in the place of instruction, and the listener too will benefit his soul rather than harm it.
If, merely because she turned back, Lot’s wife was changed and became a pillar of salt instead of a woman,
You, human being, for your part, do not let your soul change from being useful to being useless because of hypocrisy.

it is the ruin of the souls of people, both rulers and those they rule, to say, “The person at fault in some matter will be upset with me if I rebuke him.” You fool, is it not better for people to be upset with you than for God to be angry with you along with them?
How will he not be angry if you tolerate those who do improper things in his holy places, concerning which he commanded through Moses, “You shall show reverence for my holy places”?
For we truly ought to tremble and be in awe before the holy places, that is, the church of God, which the blessed Jacob saw beforehand and was afraid.

As it is written, “He came upon a place and slept there. He had a dream, and there was a ladder whose top reached up to heaven, with the angels going up and coming down on it, while the Lord stood above it.”
And afterward he said, “Jacob was afraid, and he declared, ‘This is the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.’”
What, then, is the place containing the ladder whose top reaches up to heaven, if not the church of God? In it alone is the road that leads up to heaven, and above it God stands.
It was also this that the patriarch saw when he said in fear, “This is the house of God.”
And
“This is the gate of heaven.”
For there is no other way to go to heaven except through the church alone, which God commands us to revere and from which he commands us to cast out those who sin.
For he is indignant at all times, saying, “Friend, how did you come in here without wearing wedding clothes?”
This voice was not threatening us in anger only concerning the place to which we will go.
Rather, even now it cries out still more loudly, “People, or friends,
How did you enter these places without purity, without truth, without keeping the commandments, and without deeds befitting your presence in them?

Let a spirit or an angel come down from heaven, sent by God, and stand in just one of our assemblies, and let him separate those who have no wedding clothes from among those who have them and even have extra ones on—how greatly they will be put to shame!
Or how will their mouths not also be shut, like the one of whom it was said, “But his mouth was shut”?
Or did the Lord speak words that he would not carry out?
And why have we disobeyed what is written and not hated the garment stained by the flesh, so as not to put it on?

The garment is exposed—or those garments which it is not fitting for us to wear when praying to God or serving him. These are the garments of sexual immorality, defilement, and violence, whose length, width, and [?] consist of every kind of evil.
The one who spreads them out or measures them is the master of wickedness, the devil.
Those who work on them with him are those who sin.
The loom on which they weave is the lawless heart.
The beating tools are the struggles against sound teaching.
The [?] and the [?] are stubbornness and hard-heartedness.
The threads for weaving and all their equipment are grumbling, gossip, and slander.
The [?] are lack of instruction and disobedience, and, still more, the teachings of demons.
Those who allow these tattered garments to be worked on in their house are the souls of foolish and senseless people,
What do we have to do with Satan’s sins and the deeds of those about whom it was written, “They set up a spider’s web”?
until those looking for you bury you in the mire of sin, so that the speaker in the place of instruction may rejoice, and the listener, in turn, may benefit his soul and not harm it.
If Lot’s wife was transformed merely for turning back, becoming a pillar of salt instead of a woman,
then you too, human being, must not let your soul be transformed through hypocrisy, becoming useless instead of useful.

What destroys the souls of people, both rulers and those they rule, is saying, “The person who is at fault in some matter will be offended with me if I rebuke him.” Fool, is it not better for people to be offended with you than for God to be angry with you along with them?

How could he not be angry if you tolerate those who do what is improper in his holy places? These are the places about which he also commanded through Moses, “You shall show reverence for my holy places.”
For it is truly fitting to tremble and shudder before the holy places—that is, the church of God, which the blessed Jacob foresaw and was afraid.

As it is written, “He came upon a place and slept there. He had a dream, and there was a ladder whose top reached up to heaven, with angels going up and coming down on it. And the Lord stood firmly above it.”
And afterward he said, “Jacob was afraid, and he declared, ‘This is the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.’”

What, then, is the place containing the ladder whose top reaches up to heaven, if not the church of God? She alone contains the road that leads up to heaven. She is the one above whom God stands firmly.
She is also the one the patriarch saw when he said in fear, “This is the house of God.”
And
“This is the gate of heaven.”
For there is no other way to go to heaven except through the church alone. God commands that she be treated with reverence and that those who sin be thrown out of her.
For he is indignant at all times, saying, “Friend, how did you come in here without wearing a wedding garment?”
This voice was not threatening us in anger only about the place to which we shall go.
Rather, even now it cries out all the more, “People—or friends—
how did you enter these places without being clothed in purity, truth, obedience to the commandments, and deeds worthy of your presence in them?”

Let a spirit or an angel come down from heaven, sent by God, and stand in just one of our assemblies. Let him separate those who are not wearing wedding garments from among those who have them and wear them in abundance. How greatly they would be put to shame!
Or how could they fail to shut their mouths, like the one of whom it was said, “But he remained silent”?
Or has the Lord spoken words that he will not carry out?
And why have we disobeyed what is written, failing to hate the garment defiled by the flesh so as not to put it on?
The garment, then—or those garments—is clearly identified: what it is not proper for us to wear while praying to God or serving him. These are: [?]
